cues.en: Welcome to the second major content section of this course.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到本課程第二個主要內容單元。

cues.en: Limits are really the introduction to calculus, and in fact, pretty much all of calculus is just built up from limits.
cues.zh: 極限就是真正踏入微積分的入口；事實上，幾乎整個微積分都是由極限建立起來的。

cues.en: A lot of important definitions and calculus are based on limits, including derivatives and integrals.
cues.zh: 微積分中很多重要定義都以極限為基礎，包括導數和積分。

cues.en: So you can imagine that limits are pretty foundational.
cues.zh: 所以你可以想見，極限是相當根本的概念。

cues.en: Fortunately, though, limits are also pretty simple, conceptually and in many cases, certainly not always.
cues.zh: 幸好，極限的概念也相當簡單，而且在很多情況下，當然不是每次，

cues.en: But in many times the limits of functions at particular points are pretty easy to calculate.
cues.zh: 函數在特定位置的極限都很容易計算。

cues.en: Now, I want to start this section by introducing something called Zeno's Paradox.
cues.zh: 這一節一開始，我想介紹所謂的芝諾悖論。

cues.en: Actually, there are several distinct but related paradoxes that Zeno gifted humanity with, and this one in particular is relevant for understanding limits.
cues.zh: 其實芝諾留給人類好幾個不同但相關的悖論，其中這個特別有助於理解極限。

cues.en: I think this particular paradox is sometimes called the paradox of Achilles and the tortoise or the turtle.
cues.zh: 我想這個悖論有時叫作阿基里斯與烏龜悖論。

cues.en: So imagine the great Achilles and a turtle are in a race.
cues.zh: 想像偉大的阿基里斯和一隻烏龜在賽跑。

cues.en: Now, you might think that the most famous runner in all of human storytelling would be faster than a turtle.
cues.zh: 你可能會覺得，人類故事裡最有名的跑者，應該比烏龜快。

cues.en: But Achilles is super lazy, and he says, You know what?
cues.zh: 但阿基里斯超懶，他說：「你知道嗎？

cues.en: I'm not going to run straight to the finish line.
cues.zh: 我不打算直接跑到終點。

cues.en: Instead, I'm just going to hang out here.
cues.zh: 我就在這裡待著。

cues.en: And when the turtle gets halfway to the finish line, then I will run as fast as I can to catch up to the turtle.
cues.zh: 等烏龜走到終點前的一半，我再全速跑去追上牠。」

cues.en: So the turtle gets halfway across the race, Achilles runs and catches up with him, but by the time he gets there, the turtle is still going.
cues.zh: 於是烏龜走完一半賽程，阿基里斯跑去追上牠，但等他到了，烏龜也還在繼續前進。

cues.en: And then Achilles says, Nah, you know, I want to rest.
cues.zh: 阿基里斯又說：「不了，我想休息。

cues.en: I need a break.
cues.zh: 我需要喘口氣。」

cues.en: So Achilles says, I'm going to do the same thing when the turtle gets halfway from here, which is already midway, So halfway to the finish line, then I will run as fast as I can to catch up to the
cues.zh: 所以他說：「我再做一次，等烏龜從這裡，也就是已經過半的位置，再走完剩下路程的一半，我才全速跑去追上

cues.en: turtle.
cues.zh: 烏龜。」

cues.en: And, well, you can see what's happening here.
cues.zh: 你可以看出這裡發生什麼事。

cues.en: Each time the turtle decreases the distance to the finish line and then Achilles has to catch up.
cues.zh: 每次烏龜都縮短了與終點的距離，阿基里斯才去追。

cues.en: But he's always a little bit behind the turtle.
cues.zh: 但他總是落後烏龜一點點。

cues.en: And now here's the paradox If you consider that the distance to the finish line is always decreasing
cues.zh: 悖論就在這裡：如果到終點的距離總是

cues.en: by a factor of one half of the rest of the distance to the finish line, neither of these guys will ever finish the race.
cues.zh: 減少為剩餘距離的一半，他們兩個永遠都跑不完。

cues.en: They will get closer and closer.
cues.zh: 他們會越來越接近。

cues.en: Eventually they're going to start moving in like just a couple of pico meters at a time.
cues.zh: 到最後，每次可能只前進幾皮公尺。

cues.en: But they never actually get finished.
cues.zh: 但他們始終不會真的完成比賽。

cues.en: They never reach the finish line.
cues.zh: 永遠到不了終點。

cues.en: Okay, so what's the point here?
cues.zh: 好，這裡的重點是什麼？

cues.en: How does this relate to limits?
cues.zh: 和極限有什麼關係？

cues.en: Well, the idea of limits is to understand how a function behaves when it gets really, really, really,
cues.zh: 極限的想法，就是理解當函數非常、非常、

cues.en: really, really close to a certain value without actually touching that value.
cues.zh: 非常接近某個值，卻沒有真的碰到那個值時，會有什麼行為。

cues.en: So in this analogy, the value is the end of the race.
cues.zh: 在這個比喻裡，那個值就是比賽終點。

cues.en: And when we're computing the limit, we never actually see what happens to the function at that exact point.
cues.zh: 計算極限時，我們其實不會去看函數在那個確切位置發生什麼事。

cues.en: Instead, the limit tells us what happens as we get closer and closer and closer and closer and closer until we are an infinitesimal distance from that point.
cues.zh: 極限告訴我們的是：當我們越來越接近，直到和那個點只差一個無窮小距離時，會發生什麼事。

cues.en: Okay, so this is a story I would like you to keep in mind.
cues.zh: 好，我希望你記住這個故事。

cues.en: And as you're going through this section, I hope it will help you understand the concept of a limit.
cues.zh: 在學習這一節時，希望它能幫你理解極限的概念。

cues.en: We're also going to implement limits in we're going to compute limits in numpy using this analogy.
cues.zh: 我們也會用這個比喻，在 NumPy 中實作、計算極限。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: And also just for your personal edification, the Zeno's paradox in general is that you keep approaching a target without ever actually reaching it.
cues.zh: 順便讓你多了解一點，芝諾悖論大致上就是：你不斷接近目標，卻始終沒有真正到達。

cues.en: It's a really interesting paradox.
cues.zh: 這是個很有趣的悖論。

cues.en: There's multiple implications and interpretations.
cues.zh: 有許多不同的含意與詮釋。

cues.en: If you're curious, you can read more about it, but well, I'm not going to go any deeper into Zeno's paradox than what I just did.
cues.zh: 有興趣的話可以多讀一些，不過我不會再比剛才更深入探討芝諾悖論。

cues.en: I just wanted to find a memorable way to express the idea that you keep getting closer and closer to a point without actually touching that point.
cues.zh: 我只是想用一個好記的方式，表達你不斷接近某個點，卻沒有真的碰到那個點的想法。

cues.en: And that is the idea that underlies limits as well as derivatives and integrals.
cues.zh: 這也正是極限，以及導數、積分背後的概念。

cues.en: With that introduction out of the way, I hope you enjoy working through this section.
cues.zh: 介紹就到這裡，希望你喜歡這一節的學習。

cues.en: I hope you find it fun and also educational.
cues.zh: 希望你覺得有趣，也有所收穫。
